player.design_purpose: move_speed_mps sets the pace of positioning against enemies whose speeds are below. melee_reach_m is how far in front of the player a single-target strike connects. cone_degrees is the first-person area-strike arc (D-012): 'area' means the slice of the horde you are facing, which is why training mobs into a bunch pays.

excited_boar.design_purpose: LF-3 Red boar replaces its bite with one warned nearby release. The one-second planted windup lets ordinary walking clear the exact 3.2m ring; 1.1s planted recovery rewards returning to attack. Six fire damage, no burn or immunity. Cover, stagger and freeze remain answers. Release duration shows the one contact, never repeated ticks.

retained_boar.design_purpose: LF-3 Blue boar holds a straight six-metre charge for one second without tracking. The 1.1m half-width lane covers real body contact at 20/60 physics ticks and teaches a sidestep; 0.4s travel can catch late straight retreat, solid cover stops the body, and 1.5s planted recovery rewards the flank. One six-damage physical contact per charge, never Frost or a root. Stagger/freeze cancel it.

melee.design_purpose: Slower than the player so kiting works, but relentless while you stay near (D-012 training); gives up only when you genuinely leave (give_up_distance_m).

projectile.design_purpose: Aim commits at windup start: no leading or homing. INT-05B speed gives about 0.39 seconds of flight at preferred range, so straight retreat no longer outruns the finite shot; the unchanged 0.6-second charge and lateral dodge remain. Radius sets physical clearance, range bounds misses, muzzle height sets launch point; trail, colour and glow make charge/flight readable. Solid bodies stop the shot; damage and mark apply only on player contact.

ranged.design_purpose: Keeps its distance and fires committed fire shots. Sidestep its charge or flight, use solid cover, or close on it; a landed shot still marks for the hounds.

fast.design_purpose: Harry slows a bitten player by verb_strength for verb_seconds; marked by an archer, hounds sprint. Keep the owner-approved 5.5 m/s chase. INT-05B windup_advance_m is a collision-respecting 1.1m step over the existing bite charge, committed to its starting direction so straight walking can be caught. attack_arc_degrees limits the bite to that forward sector: a deliberate sidestep, distance, cover or stagger still avoids it. Slow reduces the step. give_up_distance_m keeps escape a meaningful disengagement.

shrieker.design_purpose: The aggro-chainer: hangs back at preferred distance and screams every scream_period_seconds, waking every idle mob within scream_radius_m (D-012's Zombies-wave builder). Weak in the bite; the threat is who it invites. Killing it first is the play.

lurker.design_purpose: Root (Wave 8 slice 1): a grab from the mud holds you verb_seconds unless you dash out of it; an archer or a wisp behind it gets free shots. Slow and long-armed: it cannot catch you, but it holds ground you want.

projectile.design_purpose: A broader, slightly slower mote distinguishes the mobile kindler from the archer. INT-05B speed/range let a committed shot catch straight retreat from preferred distance; the existing half-second charge remains dodgeable. No leading or homing; solid cover stops contact. Radius controls clearance, max range bounds misses, muzzle height sets launch point, trail/colour/glow control readability.

skirmisher.design_purpose: A ranged mob that moves: keeps six metres and pecks. Faster than the archer, thinner than anything.

knight.design_purpose: A heavy melee walk with a long windup: the hit is readable, the body is not.

guard.design_purpose: The husk (Wave 8 slice 1, equal threat, different shape): slow, heavy, and its front takes verb_strength less from anything inside verb_arc_degrees of its facing until a stagger drops the guard. Flank it, stagger it, or pierce past it. Slower than the whelp, harder when it lands - the same danger in a different shape.

swarm.design_purpose: The crawler (Wave 8 slice 1): weak alone, and every other crawler within verb_radius_m adds verb_strength to its bite, to verb_cap - the dark's count is its threat. Area strikes and barbs are the answer; a corridor is a mistake.

grazer.design_purpose: flees turns the state machine around: within aggro range the animal runs, beyond give_up it settles; it never attacks.

boss.design_purpose: The breath telegraph must be long enough to read and MOVE: the cone is dodged spatially (step or dash out of it), never by invulnerability. Resistance preparation stays mandatory because a horde fight will eventually catch you inside a cone.

skills.design_purpose: Dash is pure movement (D-012): in first person, position is the defence - step or dash out of the breath cone, outpace the train. No invulnerability frames; distance and cooldown live in skills.json.

prototype_frost_orb.design_purpose: Space-and-time of the orb (ADR-0003): slow enough to lead the train with, fork_range_m decides how loose a bunch still connects

prototype_ember_bolt.design_purpose: The bolt is quick and thin next to the orb: a sniping projectile whose skill is the ignite, not the lead. fork_range_m only matters once a Forks roll teaches it to split.

prototype_bow_shot.design_purpose: The arrow: the fastest thing in the air, thin, and long in the range - a Ranger leads nothing, they pick.

prototype_frost_nova.design_purpose: A cone delivery that is a full ring: cone_degrees 360 overrides the player's first-person arc for this skill (its radius is base_area_radius in skills.json, like every cone). Everything within the ring is chilled, behind you included - the panic button.

prototype_shatter.design_purpose: Shatter is a full ring around the caster, like the nova: you stand in the frozen train and cash it in.

prototype_fan_shot.design_purpose: Arrow flight/clearance/range; fan_degrees is the angle between arrows. shared_hits makes one fan hit each enemy once, so spread is coverage rather than point-blank multiplication.

prototype_bodkin_shot.design_purpose: A narrow long arrow for lining up pursuers. Speed controls leading, radius the clearance, range the reach; the skill owns its two pierces.

prototype_driving_blow.design_purpose: The driving strike reaches further than an ordinary swing; arc in skills.json supplies its narrow width. Reach supports scale this distance.

prototype_reaping_sweep.design_purpose: Broad forward coverage for a bleeding front; does not reach behind the player.

prototype_cinderburst.design_purpose: A slower projectile that explodes at contact or range end. impact_burst replaces the direct hit with one radius hit. Pierce continues to another contact; forks launch toward untouched enemies; one cast chain never hits an enemy twice. Surface offset keeps the blast just outside solid cover.

prototype_ashfall.design_purpose: Maximum aimed surface distance and delay before the fixed mark explodes. Offset puts the mark just outside the struck surface. Live burst cap bounds stacked delayed casts; reaching it refuses a new cast without spending its cooldown.

design_purpose: round_seconds is the bridge between the sim's round-based encounter (the balance oracle) and real time: attack_period_rounds, breath periods and skill cooldowns become seconds by multiplying by it. Everything else here is time-and-space feel that the round model cannot express; damage, life and mitigation never live in this file (ADR-0003).

horde.design_purpose: D-012 stupid-zombie horde feel. jump_speed_mps (owner playtest, 2 Sep 2026: mobs got stuck on the 3D world's one-block steps, easy kills, less fun): a chaser blocked by a ledge in its path hops at this take-off speed - clears one block, not two, so cliffs and two-high walls still stop the train. Separation makes chasers push apart into a physical train instead of stacking, so bunching them is a skill. give_up_seconds is how long the player must stay beyond a chaser's give_up_distance_m before it loses interest - no eternal aggro, no instant leash. vertical_reach_m is the 3D world's rule (owner playtest, 2 Sep 2026: invisible damage from cave dwellers under the floor): a mob only aggroes on, attacks, and keeps chasing a player within this vertical band - nothing bites through rock, and a target it cannot reach for give_up_seconds is dropped. Population (owner playtest 3 Sep 2026: crowds lagged a good PC): max_live_mobs is the cap on mobs alive at once - packs beyond it wait to wake; a woken pack whose members are all idle, unhurt for sleep_after_seconds and sleep_range_m from the player goes back to sleep (its survivors return when you do). Neighbour queries run on a spatial grid, so cost follows the crowd, not its square. The train (Wave 7 slice 2; the owner, 4 Sep 2026: density should be the threat): a bite that follows bites from other mobs inside train_window_seconds lands train_bonus_per_hit harder per earlier mouth, to train_max_bonus - a lone whelp is a chore, three together are a problem, and pack count is what density means.

noise.design_purpose: Noise (Wave 7 slice 1; the owner, 4 Sep 2026: the felt density must answer what you do). Every source kind carries a radius: a press on a tree or a rock (work), a blow on a set wedge (strike), a boulder cracking (rock_crack), a tree coming down (tree_fall), a hit landing either way (fight), and the shrieker's horn (horn, slice 3). Within it every idle mob wakes and every dormant pack takes shape and comes; the shrieker's scream generalised to the world. A source inside a closed room carries muffle of its radius - walls are why the house matters at night. Chopping at dusk is a decision; a fight is a beacon; the tree you fell is heard across the meadow. The horn (Wave 7 slice 3): a shrieker's kill may leave its horn (world.json loot; the pack carries one); X blows it and everything within horn's radius comes at once - a map you open on your own terms, for the drop tables' best - and it rings horn_cooldown_seconds before it will blow again.
